lines.text: The LORD tells Joshua to choose twelve men, one from each tribe, to take stones from the middle of the Jordan.
The stones become a memorial, and the Israelites carry twelve stones to the camp, while Joshua sets up twelve more in the Jordan.
The priests wait on the far bank while the people cross, and then about 40,000 armed troops cross into the plains of Jericho.

wrong_details.wrong: The priests wait on the far bank
wrong_details.true: The priests stood in the middle of the Jordan until the people finished crossing

lines.text: The priests come up from the Jordan, the waters return, and the people camp at Shittim, where Joshua sets up the twelve stones.
Joshua says the Jordan dried up so all peoples would know the LORD's hand is mighty, and the Amorite and Canaanite kings' hearts melt.
